note: Each planned metric's core mechanism split into 4 fixed parts before any rival was tagged. A rival sits on the bullseye ring equal to the number of parts it has (yes = 1, partial = 0.5); 4 of 4 = the centre = the mechanism is taken. Rivals are the closest sources the audit-novelty runs named, tagged by fresh agents with verbatim quotes.

claims.claim: At every step, the continuous 3D quantities and tool outputs the agent computes are graded against exact simulator state.

parts.text: grades intermediate steps or stated intermediate beliefs, not only the final answer
the graded quantity is a continuous 3D value or a tool output (metric depth, distance, mask, 6-DoF camera pose), not a discrete label or grid cell
the truth is exact environment or simulator state, not a human label or model judge
graded at every step of an interactive, multi-step episode

claims.verdict_note: 2026-10-02 audit: a combination of Theory of Space, EMRD, SpaMEM and OST-Bench; at most narrowed to metric 3D quantities in one agent-driven episode

claims.claim: Camera-pose twins: the same 3D scene re-rendered from a changed camera so the answer flips, each answer checked against exact state, scored as a pair.

parts.text: two or more items are scored jointly (credit only if both or all are right)
the items differ by one controlled change that flips the correct answer
the controlled change is a camera or viewpoint change of the same 3D scene
each answer is checked against exact ground truth, not only for agreement between the two answers

claims.verdict_note: survives only for camera-pose twins checked against exact state

claims.claim: Among correct final answers, the share whose stated intermediate steps are wrong against exact state.

parts.text: looks only at items whose final answer is correct
inspects the model's stated intermediate reasoning or steps
reports how often the reasoning is wrong or not what produced the answer
the intermediate steps are checked against exact ground truth values

rivals: Measuring Faithfulness in CoT (Lanham et al.)
claims.verdict_note: the rate itself is ProcessBench's share of correct answers with a wrong step (also 2502.06217); AGQA-Decomp uses the name with exact step truth; checking steps against simulator state is an add-on

claims.claim: Replace one tool at a time with exact simulator output and measure the accuracy gain.

parts.text: replaces a component, module or tool with ground-truth or oracle output
does so for one component at a time
measures the change in final task accuracy or success
splits the total gain across several tools, including their combinations

claims.verdict_note: mostly decoration; only the multi-tool split is unseen

claims.claim: Partial credit for numeric answers by relative error, with category tolerances.

parts.text: gives partial credit for numeric answers
the credit depends on the relative error to the true value
uses several thresholds or a decaying curve, not a single cut-off
uses different tolerances per question category
